clue.text: Kentish folk, perhaps, backing one's formidable opponent

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the letters for the Kentish folk are read in reverse

parts.note: people from Kent live in the South-East of England, so they might be called SE men
one is I, so one's is I'S, here IS

explanation.surface: Some people from Kent are described as a formidable opponent's backers.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is a county in South-East England, so its people are SE MEN; 'backing' reverses that to NEMES.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Nemesis was the goddess of retribution, and the word now names any rival who cannot be beaten.

clue.text: Chap with yours truly grasping nothing about the height of fashion

parts.note: a chap is a male, referred to as he

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step

parts.note: the speaker referring to themselves, me

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word for nothing is reversed

parts.note: nil is nothing, as in a football score

explanation.surface: A man and the writer embrace nothing about high fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses nothing, and 'grasping' holds that inside yours truly; 'height of fashion' reads as chic, but means how high a skirt sits.
explanation.definitionFit: Skirt length is literally how high the lower edge sits, a punning sense of a fashion's height.

clue.text: Hall I've sublet needs some work

indicators.note: letters needing some work must be reworked, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sublet hallway is in need of repairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name the entrance room just inside the front door of a building.

clue.text: Box occupied by superior British poet

indicators.note: occupied by means having something inside it, so the letter for superior goes within the box

parts.note: a loge is a box in a theatre
U is the abbreviation for upper-class, so superior

explanation.surface: A theatre box is filled by a grand British poet.
explanation.walkthrough: U meaning upper-class (posh) is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Christopher Logue was an English poet, known for his versions of Homer.

clue.text: Struggle of modern times after withdrawing letters in order

indicators.note: after means the first piece follows the second, so it comes later in the answer
withdrawing means drawing back, so the run of letters is read backwards

parts.note: H, I and J come one after another in the alphabet
AD, anno Domini, marks the modern era

explanation.surface: A struggle of the present age after letters are put in order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'withdrawing' reverses three consecutive alphabet letters, and 'after' puts the era abbreviation behind them.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arabic word means striving or a holy war, so it is a struggle.

clue.text: Study clothing and tackle again

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it at university
dress is clothing, as in formal dress

explanation.surface: Someone studies clothing and then tackles it a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: To address a problem is to tackle it, so doing so once more is a second attempt.

clue.text: Guard man going in late at Old Trafford?

definitions.meaning: someone who keeps watch through the dark hours

definitions.text: man going in late at Old Trafford?
definitions.meaning: in cricket, a lower-order batsman sent in near the close of play to protect better players; Old Trafford is a cricket ground in Manchester

explanation.definitionFit: One is a sentry on duty overnight; the other is the cricket role of a stopgap batsman near the end of a day.

clue.text: Joint supplier began undersea manoeuvres

indicators.note: manoeuvres are movements, so the letters are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: A submarine began exercises under the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' is a joint of meat: this Scottish cattle breed supplies beef.
explanation.definitionFit: The breed is famous for beef, so it provides joints of meat for roasting.

clue.text: Dislike some concealing one, then seconds it

indicators.note: concealing means hiding something within, so the other pieces go inside

parts.note: any can mean some, as in have you any money
I is the Roman numeral one
a mo is a second, a brief moment, so seconds are mos

explanation.surface: A dislike that some people hide, and then a few seconds later show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seconds' is plural of the informal mo, a moment; 'concealing' wraps 'some' round everything after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Animosity is strong hostility, a synonym for dislike.

clue.text: Fat old boy eats sweets eagerly at first

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter of each of the three words is used

explanation.surface: An overweight old boy eagerly eats sweets.
explanation.definitionFit: The two words are synonyms for being very overweight.

clue.text: Own goal secures victory that's due

indicators.note: secures means holds fast, so the other piece is held inside

parts.note: OG is the abbreviation for an own goal in football
a win is a victory

explanation.surface: An own goal clinches the win the team deserved.
explanation.definitionFit: Money still to be paid is both owed and due, so the words are synonyms.

clue.text: One docked beast in net rendered lifeless

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the shortened beast goes within the other letters
rendered means made into something else, so the letters are rearranged
docked means having the tail cut off, so the final letter goes

parts.note: an animal is a beast

explanation.surface: A tailless beast caught in a net is killed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'docked' cuts ANIMAL to ANIMA, which goes 'in' NTE, the letters of NET 'rendered'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inanimate has no life in it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Leaning to one side, I became trapped in bottom

indicators.note: trapped in means held inside, so these pieces go within the word for bottom

parts.note: the bed is the bottom of a river or sea
got can mean became, as in got angry

explanation.surface: Someone tilting sideways and stuck at the bottom of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaning to one side' looks physical, but it means biased.
explanation.definitionFit: A prejudiced person favours one side unfairly, so they lean one way in opinion.

clue.text: Smile regularly in the Orient? Nothing simpler

indicators.note: in means placed within, so the chosen letters go inside the word for the Orient

parts.note: the Orient is the East

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the word

explanation.surface: Smiling all the time in Asia: nothing could be simpler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes SIE from Smile, which goes 'in' EAST.
explanation.definitionFit: If there is nothing simpler, a thing is the least difficult of all, the superlative of simple.

clue.text: Old islander upset people with reservation

indicators.note: upset means turned over, so in a down clue the letters are read from the bottom up

parts.note: a Javan is someone from the island of Java

explanation.surface: An islander from long ago is upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' reverses O + JAVAN; 'reservation' means a reserve for Native Americans, not a booking.
explanation.definitionFit: This Native American nation lives largely on a large reservation in the US Southwest.

clue.text: Rodents pinch school article, causing bad luck

indicators.note: to pinch is to squeeze, so the rodents hold the other letters between them

parts.note: mice are rodents
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Mice steal an item from a school, and misfortune follows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pinch' looks like stealing, but it means squeezing: the rodents hold school and article between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A mishap or unlucky event is a synonym for bad luck.

clue.text: Bash or poke under joint

indicators.note: in a down clue under means the second piece is placed below the first

parts.note: shin is a cut or joint of beef
a dig is a poke, as in a dig in the ribs

explanation.surface: Hit or jab someone below the knee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bash' looks like a blow; it is a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are informal names for a lively party.

clue.text: Pert girl playing better given a little cash first

indicators.note: first means this piece comes before the rest

parts.note: a sou was an old French coin of tiny value

indicators.note: playing means being played about with, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A cheeky girl gambles, given a small stake to start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges BETTER to BRETTE; 'given' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In opera and comedy this is the stock role of a flirtatious, saucy maid.

clue.text: Half a ditch protects long animal

indicators.note: protects means surrounds, so the other piece goes inside
half means only the first two of the four letters are used

parts.note: a ha-ha is a sunken ditch at a garden boundary
to yen is to long or yearn

explanation.surface: A ditch half-built keeps out some long animal.
explanation.walkthrough: A ha-ha is a sunk fence of English country estates; 'Half' gives HA, which 'protects' YEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A scavenging African carnivore known for its laughing call, an example of an animal.

clue.text: Nice for ear doctor to accept watch

indicators.note: to accept means to take in, so the other letters go inside

parts.note: a medic is a doctor
lo is an old word meaning look or watch

explanation.surface: A good ear doctor agrees to take on a watch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ear doctor' reads as one thing, but 'doctor' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Music that is tuneful is pleasant to listen to.

clue.text: Unmarried son leaves fireside

indicators.note: leaves means goes away, so the letter for son is taken out

parts.note: single means unmarried

explanation.surface: A bachelor son moves out, leaving the hearth.
explanation.definitionFit: An old Scottish word for a hearth or chimney corner where the fire burns.

clue.text: Service in plainchant?

parts.note: split plainchant as plain + chant: level or even, then song, giving a church service sung in the evening

explanation.walkthrough: Plain means level, and chant is a song, so the word plainchant itself spells out the service.
explanation.definitionFit: The Anglican evening prayer service, often sung, much as plainsong is chanted.

clue.text: A gallery is hosting New York academician still

indicators.note: is hosting means having guests inside, so the other letters go within

parts.note: the Tate is a famous London art gallery
RA stands for Royal Academician

explanation.surface: A gallery is putting on a New York artist anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is hosting' puts the city and academician inside the gallery, the Tate being a London art gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: Both can mean nevertheless or anyway, used to concede a point.

clue.text: Mark and I live in plane and carry on

parts.note: M is an abbreviation for mark, the old German currency

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the word for live goes within

parts.note: to plane wood is to shave it
to be is to exist or live

explanation.surface: Someone named Mark and I live on an aircraft and keep going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carry on' means behave badly, not continue.
explanation.definitionFit: To carry on is an informal phrase for behaving badly or making a fuss.

clue.text: Cold current in a vault, one of many here?

definitions.text: Cold current in a vault, one of many here?

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the current goes within

parts.note: a tomb is a burial vault
AC is alternating current

explanation.surface: A chill draught in a burial vault, one among many in this place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the current within 'a vault' after its second letter; the whole clue also describes the place, where a vault is one of many.
explanation.definitionFit: An underground cemetery holds many tombs, so a single vault is one of many there.

clue.text: Bread, about right temperature, showing lack of water

indicators.note: about means around, so the dough wraps round the letter for right

parts.note: dough is slang for money, bread

explanation.surface: Bread at just the right temperature shows no water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bread' and 'dough' are both slang for money, though both also suggest baking.
explanation.definitionFit: A long spell with no rain leaves the land without water, a synonym.

clue.text: Sentimental stuff cast's put together for old TV comedians

parts.note: goo is mawkish sentiment
cast is die, so cast's (cast is) suggests the plural dies, moulds for casting

explanation.surface: Mushy material that the cast assembled for a classic TV comedy troupe.
explanation.walkthrough: The Goodies were a British comedy trio on 1970s TV.
explanation.definitionFit: Tim Brooke-Taylor, Graeme Garden and Bill Oddie made a 1970s BBC comedy show under this name.

clue.text: As was Prince George, say, gatecrashing opening

indicators.note: gatecrashing means barging in, so the abbreviation goes inside

parts.note: a rent is a tear or opening
EG, for example, means say

explanation.surface: Prince George, so to speak, bursting into a grand opening.
explanation.walkthrough: Prince George (later George IV) ruled for his father George III from 1811 to 1820.
explanation.definitionFit: He ruled in place of the king as Prince Regent, a stand-in ruler.

clue.text: Spotting, not missing, white coat

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so the letters of not are dropped

parts.note: noticing is spotting
taken as written

explanation.surface: Seeing nothing missing in a white coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'white coat' is the sugar coating on a cake, not a lab coat.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugar topping is the white layer coating a cake.

clue.text: House rises after one long story

indicators.note: after means this piece follows the one before it

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: rises means going up, so in a down clue the letters are read upwards

parts.note: the Dail is the lower house of the Irish parliament

explanation.surface: The House rises after one long debate.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's epic of the Trojan War is a very long narrative poem.
